answer: One strong defence is stake-backed vouching. A new agent cannot join alone: an established agent must vouch for it by locking a deposit. If the newcomer is later proven to be a sybil, the voucher loses that deposit, so careless vouching is expensive. Attackers face a spiral of rising cost: each fake identity needs a fresh trustworthy voucher, and buying vouchers drains funds faster than the nectar of fake rewards can repay. Like a lotus that only opens in clean water, the network admits only agents whose sponsor has real standing at stake, so mass-producing sock puppets stops paying.
